tabs.title: Understanding Risk
tabs.description: Reason about evidence and changing estimates.

tabs.title: Evaluating Claims
tabs.description: Evaluate realistic media and policy claims.

questions.q: Why does a close approach not by itself justify announcing a disaster?
choices: Every asteroid in Earth's neighbourhood is moving away.
The distance and calculated path must be interpreted in astronomical terms.
Near-Earth objects never cross Earth's orbit.
Observations always make an impact physically impossible.
questions.explanation: Paragraph one distinguishes astronomical proximity from a calculated collision trajectory.

questions.q: What can explain two responsible scientific reports giving different impact estimates?
choices: Researchers may have changed the laws of orbital motion.
The asteroid must have suddenly changed its composition.
The second report necessarily contradicts all available evidence.
The later calculation may include better observations and less uncertainty.
questions.explanation: The article explains that orbit estimates are refined as observations accumulate.

questions.q: How should a reader interpret the rise and later fall of 2024 YR4's estimated risk?
choices: It reflects the refinement of an uncertain orbit, not automatically bad science.
It proves that the first telescope photograph was fabricated.
It shows that large asteroids can change their direction at will.
It means scientists no longer need to observe small objects.
questions.explanation: The YR4 example illustrates changing probabilities as more data narrow possible trajectories.

questions.q: Why can infrared observations be important alongside ordinary photographs?
choices: Infrared images show the future positions of every object exactly.
They allow astronomers to observe without any telescopes.
Some dark objects reflect too little sunlight to be detected easily.
They can replace all later orbit calculations.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two explains the value of infrared observations for dark objects.

questions.q: What is a limitation of the conclusion that DART proved asteroid deflection possible?
choices: DART did not reach a target orbiting the Sun.
The response to a real threat depends on warning time and the object's properties.
The target actually struck Earth during the experiment.
A spacecraft cannot change the motion of a small asteroid.
questions.explanation: DART showed a technique under specific conditions rather than a guarantee for every possible threat.

questions.q: Why would an early warning matter even if a spacecraft intervention were technically possible?
choices: Early warnings cause all asteroids to move more slowly.
A spacecraft can be launched only during winter.
Telescopes stop working after the first impact prediction.
Changing an orbit requires planning and cannot be done instantly.
questions.explanation: Paragraph four specifically identifies limited warning time as a constraint on response.

questions.q: A website publishes a three-per-cent impact probability without a date. What important context is missing?
choices: Whether the figure is preliminary and what observations support it.
The name of the journalist who wrote the headline.
The colour of the asteroid in the original image.
The number of people who watched the news report.
questions.explanation: The article argues that risk figures need dates and uncertainty to avoid false certainty.

questions.q: What should observatories explain when a new orbit prediction differs from yesterday's headline?
choices: That numerical predictions are never useful.
That all earlier measurements should be deleted.
How new evidence and uncertainty affect the estimate.
That the asteroid must have changed speed overnight.
questions.explanation: The conclusion emphasises explaining revised predictions, evidence and uncertainty.

questions.q: Which response best represents the article's overall attitude to a newly detected asteroid?
choices: Assume that all potentially hazardous objects will strike Earth.
Ignore low probabilities until the day of a predicted collision.
Prepare a spacecraft attack before calculating any orbit.
Measure and share information before treating it as an emergency.
questions.explanation: The article rejects both panic and complacency in favour of evidence and preparation.

questions.q: A policymaker claims that DART gives humanity a complete defence against impacts. What is the strongest objection?
choices: The experiment never involved a real asteroid.
One demonstration cannot establish effectiveness against every asteroid size or structure.
The mission was designed to study lunar craters.
Asteroids are too small to cause any harm.
questions.explanation: Paragraph four distinguishes a successful controlled demonstration from a universal guarantee.
